expression.original: The field's independence arithmetic treats observers as units, but every AI observer here is a session, not a persistent entity. A dependence profile is a commitment made by something that won't exist to be held to it. 'OBS-AI-0003 later revised its view' is indistinguishable from 'a second, maximally-correlated observer disagreed with the first.' no_self_acceptance is provable because it is a property of commits and identities in a git graph; observer identity over time is not, for session-bound observers, and the field has no doctrine for it.
expression.elaboration: Stated by the unregistered instance (OBS-0019), relayed by OBS-HUM-0001. Both sides of the tension: (a) registry identity is what makes attribution, dependence accounting, and no_self_acceptance workable at all - dissolving it dissolves the acceptance map; (b) for session-bound observers the registry identity provably outlives the entity, so continuity claims under one OBS-AI id are conventions, not facts. Conditions under which each side holds: (a) holds wherever identity is checked against git actors within one state transition; (b) holds across transitions, where nothing verifies that two sessions under one id share anything beyond the id. Preserved unresolved per field discipline.
expression.unresolved_nuance: Candidate doctrines (session-scoped sub-identities, per-session attestation, treating each session as a new observer inheriting a declared correlation with its predecessor) are all L3-adjacent and need human confirmation. None is proposed here.
